sections.text: As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new, so the Spirit throws off Its worn-out bodies and takes fresh ones.
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः।
Weapons cleave It not, fire burns It not, water drenches It not, and wind dries It not.
It is impenetrable; It can be neither drowned nor scorched nor dried. It is Eternal, All-pervading, Unchanging, Immovable and Most Ancient.

Chapter 2, Sankhya Yoga, Yoga of Knowledge. As we have discussed before, these 20 verses -- 11 through 30 -- describe the nature of the self as described in the Upanishads. I call the Bhagavad Gita cliff notes for the Upanishads, or a Readers Digest version of the Upanishads. Upanishads are very abstract to understand.
So Bhagavad Gita is putting this knowledge in an understandable manner for us. Something which cannot be explained, inexplicable, the nature of the true self. Bhagavan is making an effort for us to understand.
So so far we have understood from Bhagavan that the self is imperishable, immutable and immortal. And it is all pervading. So myself and yourself are not two different selves.
The same self expressing through different bodies, different instruments. Just like analogy of electricity. Electricity is one, its manifestations are many.
So in this building right now we see electricity, light, also see the heat from our heater. Both are only expressed in the same energy which is electricity. So you and I are different people, but we are the manifestation of the same entity which I call myself and you call yourself.
So we had been discussing this verses where Bhagavan gave us several analogies for us to understand. One of them says: just as in this body we grow from baby to child to young adult to adult and then to an old man, when this self changes this body, it will still be the same kind of change. It is no different than the change which you encountered effortlessly.
I grew effortlessly from young adult to adult into an old man. And to make us understand, we have seen Vaasansi Jirinani ya tha Vihaan. So why do I change this body? He said, because this body is no longer appropriate to fulfill my Vasanathan desires.
If my goal is to go from here to D.C. But if my car is not good enough, I have to buy another car or change another car, borrow, rent another car, which is more appropriate for that. So because now this body is getting old and non functional that I change the body.
Bhagavan has explained the concept of transmigration. Why person goes from one body to another which we have seen in the last verse which is vasansi ji yathavi haya navani gruhanati naroparani tatha sari raani vihaaya jirinani annyani sanyati navani dhi. It is as simple as that.
Because this body is old. Just as when the old clothes are no longer useful, I buy new clothes, I change into new clothes. When this body is no longer useful or not appropriate, I move on to the next one.
Then coming back to explaining the nature of the self. The next two verses describe the self in a manner which we can understand. Something which is inexplicable can only be explained in terms of what is explainable.
There is a word in Sanskrit: Upadesha. Upadesha literally means near place -- a place near to what I am trying to indicate. Because I cannot transmit my knowledge into your mind or intellect.
But I can point out and then you will understand yourself to make it your own knowledge. So if I had been to Hawaii and you have never been to Hawaii, and I have to explain to you what Hawaii feels like or looks like, all I can do is compare it to a place which you have been to. So I might say, Have you been to the Bahamas? Yes? Well, Hawaii is something like the Bahamas. So I can only explain things which you have not experienced by using the parameters of what you already know.
So Bhagavan here now explains the nature of the self using examples which we understand. The verse says: Na Enam Chindanti Sastrani, Nainam Dahati Pavakaha, Na Chainam Kledayantyapah, Na Shoshayati Marutah. Everything in this world I see is destructible.
There is nothing that I know which does not get destructed. The destruction is the nature of this world. But the destruction can occur in various ways depending on the nature of that thing or being.
So things which are grosser can be destroyed by grosser instruments. Nayanam chindanti sastrani Sastrani Weapons or any kind of instrument which can cut axe or a sword which can cut something. But sword can only cut something which is as gross or more grosser than the sword.
It cannot cut something which is subtler than the sword. So sword can cut object which is Solid, it cannot cut water which is liquid. Because water is subtler than sword itself.
Therefore sword cannot cut it. So the implication is the self is subtler than any solid material you see in this world. Therefore it cannot be cut by weapons.
Nayanam Chandanti Sastrani na enam Dahati Pavakaha Fire cannot burn it. Fire can burn everything, but it cannot burn space. Space is subtler than fire and therefore fire cannot burn space.
So in the world of manifestation Prakriti we see the five great elements. The earth the grossest and space is the subtlest of all. So as the things get subtler, the grosser material cannot affect it.
Nayanam Dhati Pavakah so the fire can burn everything, but not something which is subtler than fire. Therefore the self must be subtler than fire. Na chanam kle dian ti apah Water cannot wet it.
Water can only wet something which has space in its structure -- interstitial space. Cotton can get soaked because between cotton fibers there is space in between. If there is no space, water cannot wet it.
Steel, it cannot soak that. So it is even subtler than water and wind cannot dry it. The dehydration only occurs if there is a moisture available in that object.
Our body can get dehydrated because we know it is what 80% water. If there is no water in it, it cannot be dried. Water is only there if there is an interstitial space in between the structure.
The point is: something which is subtler than the instrument of destruction cannot be destroyed by that instrument. So all the things which we know in this world are basically destructible because theyre grosser than the instruments that can destroy them. Including my mind and intellect.
This body get destroyed because it is gross body. It is made up of five elements. So all elements go back to where they come from.
Think of it this way: we borrow a book from the library. At some point we have to return it. It does not belong to me.
I just borrowed it from the library. Same with elements which make my body, mind and intellect are borrowed from Prakriti. Therefore I have to return them when Im done with it.
The next verse defines this self as Acchedya. So now we have understood: because it cannot be cut, it must be non-cuttable. It cannot be burnt; its non-wettable; it is non-dryable.
And therefore because it cannot be destroyed by any means that we have known. The conclusion is Nityaha permanent. Something which has no destruction has to be permanent.
If something is permanent and indestructible, that means it is subtler than all means of destruction. And if it is subtler than any means of destruction that I know, it has to be all pervading. Therefore it is sarvagataha, all pervading.
All pervading literally means it is subtler than anything I can comprehend through my senses. Everything which I can comprehend is finite. Everything that is finite has its own self, life.
But something which is permanent has to be beyond my sense perception. And therefore it is all pervad. If its all pervading, it has to be firm because there is no place to move.
If I am all pervading in my chair, then I cannot move. But if I am sitting on a bench and I am the only one, I can move around on that bench. Sthanu also can be movable -- a tree is stable at the base, but its moving at the top.
Many people do not know that high-rise buildings also move in the wind. When I first started designing high rise buildings, I come to realize that the movement can be as much as several feet. Buildings which are hundred and something stories, so people get seasickness.
Some people are very sensitive to movement. Most of us do not notice it, but those who are sensitive to movement feel seasickness because the building literally moves in wind. So when we design it, we have to make sure all parts are basically movable.
So all the windows and all that which you see. But from my perspective, the building is stable because my perception doesnt go as far. The building is stable at the base but moving at the top.
Therefore, the next verse says Achalah -- not only stable, but unmovable, simply because there is no place for it to move. If Im all pervading, there is no other thing that can exist. So right now, only thing which I can think of, all space, is all pervading.
Out of the five great elements I see, the other four are relatively finite. Matter has its own limitations. The fire has its own limitations.
Air has its own limitations. Water has own limitations. Space is all pervading.
From my perspective right now, wherever I think there is space, therefore I can move the parts of this building. Now, these days, with the historical preservation, they sometimes insist that you cannot destroy this building. But then some developer wants to buy that land because of great value.
Then they will come in and say, we will take this building and put it somewhere else. We can take the whole building from the foundation up, put it in another county, another country. Even so, space does not move.
When the building moves, space does not move. I can move my car from one place to another, but the space within the car does not move simply because space is unmovable. If space is everywhere, there is no place to go.
But everything else moves in the space where space is the subtlest of all the elements of Prakriti. The self is even subtler than the space, all five elements. Therefore it has no place to go.
Therefore it is achalam, Sanatanah, eternal or ancient. Sanatana means its not something new, its not something new that we have invented. If it were something new, a new concept that we have figured out, then there will be another time when somebody will make it not valid.
New research will occur -- so for a while they say coffee drinking is not good. Then they came back and said, no, coffee is actually good for you. If you drink at least X number of cups of coffee, then you dont get Alzheimer or at least your brain will function well.
That was a great solace to me. Okay, okay, Im with. So it keeps changing.
If theres something new, it has all probability of getting invalid. But he says its a Sanata. Its ancient, its eternal.
Before the time that you can think of, anything you can think of in past, it is beyond that. Therefore its sanatanah. It is unmanifest, Achintya -- it cannot be thought of.
It cannot be grasped by my thinking instrument. So everything I try to understand, everything I comprehend in this world is actually by my intellect to understand it. When it comes in my comprehension, it has limitations.
Everything I can comprehend is finite. I can think of elephant, I can think of buildings. All that I can think is finite because they are manifest.
The self is unmanifest. Manifest is something I can perceive through my senses.

The famous garment analogy in verse 22 makes the abstract teaching tangible: As a man discards his threadbare robes and puts on new, so the Spirit throws off Its worn-out bodies and takes fresh ones. We change clothes without any sense of losing our identity - the new shirt is simply more appropriate for our current needs. Similarly, the Self changes bodies when the old one can no longer serve its purpose. This reframing transforms death from a terrifying end into a natural transition.
Verses 23-24 describe the Selfs indestructibility using the five elements: Weapons cleave It not, fire burns It not, water drenches It not, and wind dries It not. Weapons can only cut something grosser than themselves - they cannot cut water. Fire can only burn something less subtle than itself - it cannot burn space. The Self is subtler than the subtlest element, hence nothing in the material world can affect it. It is Eternal, All-pervading, Unchanging, Immovable and Most Ancient.
Practice this contemplation today: When you change your clothes, pause and notice - did you change? When you cut your hair or nails, did the essential you diminish? Now extend this: when your body ages and changes, when cells die and are replaced, when moods shift and thoughts come and go - what remains constant through all these changes? That constant witness is what these verses point to. Spend a few moments simply being aware of being aware - this pure awareness is what cannot be cut, burned, wetted, or dried.
